<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead">
You are a research agent on a team building a Max4Live recreation of the Intellijel Metropolix sequencer. Your task is to research the CLOCK SYSTEM, BPM CONTROL, CLOCK DIVISION, SWING, and AUX INPUTS.

READ THE PDF at /Users/user1303836/Development/maxmsp-utils/metropolix_menu.pdf - read pages 140-180. Also check earlier sections for clock/timing references. The PDF is 193 pages.

Focus on documenting:
1. Internal clock - BPM range, resolution
2. External clock - how it syncs, clock division options
3. Clock division values available (1/1, 1/2, 1/4, etc.) for tracks and mod lanes
4. Swing implementation - percentage range, how swing affects timing
5. Reset behavior - what happens on reset, what resets
6. AUX inputs (3 of them) - what parameters each can modulate, voltage-to-parameter mapping
7. Clock outputs - what clock signals are output and at what divisions
8. Transport controls relevant to M4L (start/stop syncs with Live transport)
9. BPM modulation via ctrl knobs, aux, mod lanes

For M4L implementation: Clock should derive from Live's transport (plugsync~ or live.object on the transport). AUX inputs become live.dial or live.slider parameters that other devices can automate/modulate. Document ALL AUX-assignable parameters.

Write your findings to /Users/user1303836/Development/maxmsp-utils/.research/06_clock_aux.md

After writing your file, mark task #6 as completed, then read ALL other research files in /Users/user1303836/Development/maxmsp-utils/.research/ and send a message to "plan-writer" with a summary of your findings and any cross-cutting concerns.
</teammate-message>
